title: Stakeholder alignment cookbook for slow rollouts (working)
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight cookbook for aligning cross-functional stakeholders when we intentionally adopt slow, multi-wave rollouts (aka long-duration canaries) for latency-sensitive or high-risk features. Focus is on ceremony that reduces friction and produces explicit consensus rather than relying on implicit sign-offs.

When to use this cookbook:
- Big surface-area LLM features (rerankers, cross-model routing, model family switches) where user impact is non-trivial
- Deployments with mixed tiers (hosted + dedicated + private) where rollback cost is high
- Experiments requiring staged human review or regulatory signoff

High-level goals:
1) Make risk explicit (who accepts which risks and why)
2) Produce compact artifacts that allow quick go/no-go decisions
3) Keep a minimal, repeatable cadence so stakeholders can plan
4) Maintain an auditable signal ledger for postmortem and compliance

Core roles and responsibilities (consensus deck):
- Release Steward (owner): runs the cadence, owns decision log and tickets
- Impact SME(s): product/PM who owns user-risk hypothesis and measurement plan
- Observability Lead: defines dashboards, alerts, and pulse signals for the run
- SRE/Infra: owns capacity, fallback routes, throttle knobs and emergency revert steps
- Safety/Policy: reviews content and edge-case legal/regulatory concerns (when applicable)
- Customer Success/Support: prepares comms templates and escalations for customers
- Engineering (feature owner): provides rollout config, A/B wiring, and quick-fix PRs

Pre-launch alignment checklist (runbook template):
- One-pager hypothesis: 2–4 bullets (impact, expected delta, primary risk)
- Risk matrix: list of top 3 failure modes and mitigation for each (short paragraph)
- Measurement plan: primary signal, 2 backups, and what constitutes an automatic revert
- Capacity handshake: confirmed throughput headroom and canary throttle values
- Fallback mapping: which model/route to return to and how to switch traffic quickly
- Communication plan: who to ping and channel templates (pager, slack, email)
- Regulatory sign-off (if needed): documented acceptance from Security/Legal

Cadence (recommended minimal rhythm):
- T-3 days: Alignment workshop (30–45m) -> decision matrix + sign-off placeholders filled
- T-1 day: Dry-run rehearsal (operator walk-through of rollback and partial revert)
- Activation day: Three checkpoints (hour 0, hour 6, hour 24) with short updates
- Extended waves: Daily pulse + 48h deep review for each incremental slice

Checkpoints and consensus protocol (how decisions are made):
- Green/Amber/Red scoreboard: each checkpoint owner (Impact SME, Observability, SRE) publishes an encoded state (green/amber/red) with a 1-sentence rationale
- Consensus rule: rollout continues if no more than one Red and majority not Red and no unresolved legal or safety blocker
- Hard stop: any Red from Safety or SRE triggers immediate freeze and rollback protocol unless explicit exception documented

Signal taxonomy (examples for LLM rollouts):
- Primary signals: latency p95, error-rate (model runtime exceptions), user-visible correctness regression (evaluations on holdout prompts)
- Secondary signals: token-cost per request, queue-time, downstream consumer errors (e.g., search client failures)
- Human-review signals: sampled transcripts with scoring rubric, CS escalations count

Communication templates (short forms to paste into Slack/email):
- Activation notice: "Rolling out X -> 1%->5% over 24h. Steward: @AvaM. Watch: latency-p95, model-exceptions. Revert plan: switch to model-v1. Contact: #rollouts-page"
- Freeze notice: "HALT: Observability flagged Red on latency-p95 > 600ms AND model-exceptions spike. Steward @AvaM pausing further exposure. Next steps: SRE to assess and propose fix within 60m."

Consensus scoreboard example (one-line per checkpoint):
- Impact SME: Green — metrics trending toward expected uplift (A/B delta +0.6%)
- Observability: Amber — latency p95 +15% but within safety margin; investigating allocation
- SRE: Green — capacity stable, no infra anomalies

Post-checklist and postmortem artifacts: 
- Fill decision log (timestamped entries for each checkpoint)
- Export sampled transcripts and attach scored evals for first wave
- Cost ledger: incremental cost per 1000 requests during rollout (compare to baseline)
- Lessons: 3 bullets (what surprised us, what to change next time)

Templates to copy (in doc):
- One-pager hypothesis (title, owner, expected user impact, rollback criteria)
- Decision log CSV columns: timestamp, actor, state(G/A/R), rationale, action_taken, links
- Rehearsal script: sequence of ops for T-1 day dry run (controls to flip, metrics to read)

Open questions / unresolved tradeoffs (notes to discuss):
- How long should the default 'extended wave' be for generative features? (48h vs 7d)
- When to declare cost regressions as a signal equal-weight to correctness? (thresholds?)
- Should Legal get read-only scoreboard access or active veto for regulated releases?

Short-term follow-ups (owners):
- Leo: draft scoreboard automation in Console (dashboard + simple green/amber/red API) — due 2026-03-15
- Rina: build a short rehearsal checklist in the runbook templates page — due 2026-03-08
- Ethan: prototype a decision-log export with filters by tag and timeframe — due 2026-03-22

Notes to self: keep this cookbook intentionally prescriptive but minimal; the point is to reduce back-and-forth and convert opinions into recorded signals. Add more pre-built Slack templates once we validate the cadence across 2 live rollouts.

Appendix (links and references):
- Example: microrelease-activation-lattice and activation-sentinel playbooks (see other drive docs)
- Internal PR that added canary throttle knobs: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/391

---
Document history: created 2025-11-12; active edits by release stewards during planning sprints.
